article.Citation/Title: Smart, R. G., Storm, T., Baker, E. F. W., & Solursh, L. (1966). A controlled study of lysergide in the treatment of alcoholism. I. The effects on drinking behavior. Quarterly Journal of Studies on Alcohol, 27(3), 469-482.
article.Outcome: 34% vs 32% vs 20% gain in abstinence (lysergide vs ephedrine vs control)
article.InterventionDescription: Single 800-mcg dose of lysergide (LSD) in a hospital ward followed by a 3-hr psychotherapeutic interview; compared with 60-mg ephedrine or no-drug control, within an inpatient alcoholism program.

ae_events.Description: Two patients died during the study period; both deaths occurred after their 6-month follow-up assessments had already been completed.

article.Outcome: Primary outcome per abstract-leading precedence: the article gives no single authors-designated primary endpoint, so the SUD-behavioral outcome the abstract leads with was used — percentage gain in abstinence, reported in the abstract as 'the gain in abstinence time in the lysergide, ephedrine and control groups, respectively, was 34%; 32%; and 20%.' Note a discrepancy: the Results section (p.476) gives slightly different values for the same comparison — 'average gains of 33.7% (lysergide), 31.5% (ephedrine) and 19.6% (control)' — the abstract figures appear rounded; both are internally consistent with each other (not contradictory, just rounded differently), so no anti-fabrication flag beyond noting it. This is a 3-group (not 2-group) comparison, so it is reported as a labelled 3-way descriptor rather than a single numeric effect size.
article.SD: The paired inferential statistic for the same abstinence-gain comparison, from p.476: 'Simple analyses of variance...showed no differences between the lysergide, ephedrine and control groups in percentage gain in total abstinence (F = 0.323, p>.05).' No error/numerator degrees of freedom are printed for this specific F-test (unlike Table 2, whose df apply to the separate drinking-occasions/drunkenness-occasions ANOVAs, not to this abstinence comparison), so df is omitted rather than inferred.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: N=30 (10 lysergide, 10 ephedrine, 10 control) is the analyzed sample for all drinking-behavior comparisons, confirmed in the abstract ('30 alcoholics...were randomly selected... divided into 3 groups') and in Results ('all 30 patients were seen' at follow-up). See Retention (%) rationale for the separate question of the pre-completion enrolled/randomized total.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: 13/14 met; only 'harms' unmet — the article never describes a methodology for assessing or monitoring adverse events/safety (only incidental precautionary details such as bed restraint 'for security' and PRN chlorpromazine, plus an unattributed mortality mention with no cause or arm given). 'sample_size_power' credited on a close call: the Discussion explicitly reflects on whether N=10/group was adequate to detect the effect sizes claimed by prior uncontrolled studies ('the small number of patients used—only 10 in each group. But in previous reports the effectiveness of lysergide was so striking that 10 subjects should have demonstrated them'), which meets the field-level rule that a bare underpowered-study statement counts as 'discussed.'

ae_events.Smart 1966_AE01: Article states in the Follow-Up section (p.474): 'Two patients died during the period covered by the study but both died after their follow-up had been completed.' No cause of death, treatment-arm assignment, or temporal proximity to the drug session is given, and the authors do not label it an SAE or discuss it further anywhere in the paper. Graded Severe under the rubric (death meets the FDA-seriousness criterion by definition) with SeveritySource='rubric' rather than 'author' because no author severity/seriousness language accompanies the mention (consistent with this being a pre-1980 article, predating CTCAE). SeverityIndeterminate='Y' because causal relationship to lysergide/ephedrine, timing relative to drug exposure, and arm membership are all unreported. ArmScope is coded 'pooled' rather than 'psychedelic_arm' because arm membership of the two deceased patients is not stated and should not be assumed to be lysergide-arm-only. Coding this event at all — and consequently SafetyReported='Y', HarmsAssessed=1, MortalityMeasured=1 — is a judgment call: the study has no dedicated adverse-event/safety section, and this note could be read as routine study-accounting rather than a safety report. It is coded conservatively per the cardinal 'never understate harm' rule and the field-level instruction that any reported death generates an ae_events row, and is flagged here for human review rather than silently omitted.

config_proposal.metric: Non-significant 3-group ANOVA (multi-df F) — percentage gain in abstinence
config_proposal.measure: 34 vs 32 vs 20 (%, lysergide vs ephedrine vs control)
config_proposal.note: The primary comparison is a one-way ANOVA across three arms (df=2 numerator; error df not printed for this specific test), F=0.323, p>.05. The supported conversion methods include only single-df-numerator F; a 3-group omnibus F is not reducible to a single pairwise effect size without additional pairwise data the article does not report, so this is excluded rather than approximated.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: Non-significant omnibus test across lysergide/ephedrine/control on the abstract-leading abstinence-gain outcome; lysergide had the numerically largest gain (~34%) but was statistically indistinguishable from the active ephedrine comparator (~32%) and not clearly superior to the no-drug control (~20%), and every other reported drinking-behavior outcome (drinking occasions, drunkenness occasions, symptom checklist, clinic contacts) was also non-significant between groups — the authors' own conclusion is that lysergide 'failed as an effective adjunct to psychotherapy.'
